operations.description:
Create a new discussion board article with title, content, section assignment, and optional attachments.

This operation enables members to submit new articles to the economic/political discussion board. The article requires selection of a section (topic category), a title for identification, and content text as the main discussion body. Authors can optionally associate tags for content categorization and search discoverability.

File and image attachments can be uploaded alongside the article creation. Each attachment is stored with metadata including filename, file URL, and type classification. Attachments are linked to the article and will be automatically deleted if the article is removed.

The system enforces atomic creation: all components (article record, tag associations, attachments) are saved together or none are persisted. Upon successful creation, the article becomes immediately visible to all users in the selected section.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Execute the following steps in a single transaction:

1. Validate input data:
   - Check that title is not empty (minimum 1 character, maximum defined in validation rules)
   - Check that content is not empty (minimum 1 character)
   - Verify section_id references an existing section record
   - Validate tagIds references existing tags (create if new per tag rules)
   - Validate attachment metadata: file_name non-empty, file_type in allowed values, file_url is valid URI

2. Create article record:
   - Generate new UUID for article id
   - Set author_id from authenticated user's ID
   - Set section_id from request
   - Set title and content from request
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp

3. Process tag associations:
   - For each tagId in request, verify tag exists
   - Create economic_political_board_article_tags junction records
   - Use atomic upsert pattern if tags are auto-created

4. Process attachments:
   - For each attachment in attachmentData, create economic_political_board_attachments record
   - Link article_id as foreign key
   - Set file_name, file_url, file_type, created_at from input

5. Return response:
   - Return full article object with all fields including id, author_id, section_id, title, content, created_at, updated_at
   - Include attachment list and tag associations in response

requestBody.description: Article creation data including required fields and optional attachments

responseBody.description: Created article with all fields and associated data

operations.description:
Update an existing article's title, content, attachments, and tags.

This operation allows the article author to modify their published content. The authenticated user must be the original author of the article to perform this update. The system validates ownership before applying any changes to ensure users can only edit their own content.

The operation supports updating the article title and content body fields. File attachments can be added or removed as part of the update process. Tag associations are also modifiable, allowing the article to be re-categorized with different keywords.

This operation performs a soft delete check - the article must not have been deleted (deleted_at field must be null). If the article has been soft-deleted, the operation will fail with a 404 Not Found error. All modifications update the article's updated_at timestamp while preserving the original creation timestamp and section assignment.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the authenticated user is the article author by comparing user_id from session with author_id from article record
2. Fetch the article record by articleId from economic_political_board_articles table
3. Validate article is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
4. Apply provided update fields: title, content, or both
5. Process attachment updates based on update request (add new, remove existing)
6. Process tag updates based on update request (add new associations, remove existing)
7. Update the updated_at timestamp to current time
8. Return the complete updated article record with all relationships

responseBody.description: The complete updated article with all associated data

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the article to update

requestBody.description: Update data for the article including title, content, and attachment/tag management

prerequisites.description: Article must be created before it can be updated
Section must exist to be referenced by the article

operations.description:
Permanently remove an article from the economic/political discussion board.

This operation deletes an article along with all associated data including comments, file attachments, and tag relationships. Members can only delete articles they authored, while administrators have authority to delete any article regardless of ownership.

The deletion is permanent and irreversible. Once removed, the article and all its associated content cannot be recovered. Before deletion, the system requires explicit confirmation from the user.

When an article is deleted:
- All comments authored on this article are permanently removed
- All file attachments linked to this article are deleted from storage
- All tag associations for this article are removed from the junction table
- The article is removed from all section listings and search indexes

Authorization requirements:
- Members: Can only delete articles they authored (author_id matches current user)
- Administrators: Can delete any article on the platform regardless of ownership
operations.name: erase

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: UUID identifier of the article to be deleted

operations.specification:
DELETE operation to permanently remove an article from the system.

Database Operation:
- BEGIN TRANSACTION
- Verify article exists and is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
- Check authorization: if current user is member, validate article.author_id == current_user_id; if current user is admin, allow any article deletion
- CASCADE delete: All comments with article_id == articleId are automatically deleted via ON DELETE CASCADE
- CASCADE delete: All attachments with article_id == articleId are automatically deleted via ON DELETE CASCADE
- CASCADE delete: All ArticleTag entries with article_id == articleId are automatically deleted
- Soft delete: Set article.deleted_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (or hard delete if system policy requires permanent removal)
- If hard delete: Execute DELETE FROM economic_political_board_articles WHERE id = articleId
- Verify cascade deletes completed successfully
- COMMIT TRANSACTION

Validation Rules:
- Article ID must be valid UUID format
- Article must exist in the database
- Current user must have permission (owner or admin)
- Article must not be already deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
- If member attempting deletion, verify ownership via article.author_id

Error Handling:
- 404 Not Found: Article with specified ID does not exist
- 403 Forbidden: Current user is not the article author and does not have admin privileges
- 409 Conflict: Article has already been deleted
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid UUID format for articleId

Cascading Operations:
- All economic_political_board_comments with article_id matching the deleted article are removed
- All economic_political_board_attachments with article_id matching the deleted article are removed
- All economic_political_board_article_tags with article_id matching the deleted article are removed
- Article is permanently removed from all section listings and search indexes

Post-Deletion Actions:
- Update author's article count (decrement by 1)
- Remove article from any active search index
- Free storage space for deleted attachments
- Log deletion event for audit trail (timestamp, actor, article_id, reason if admin)

Security Considerations:
- Enforce authorization check before any deletion operation
- Never allow deletion without explicit confirmation
- Record deletion in audit log with actor identity
- Validate that cascade deletes completed successfully before committing transaction

operations.description:
Manage file attachments (add and/or remove) for a specific article in the Economic/Political Discussion Board.

This operation allows article owners to attach multiple files to their article or remove existing attachments. Each attachment can be an image or document file stored with its file URL, file type, and original file name.

The operation requires an authenticated member or administrator to execute. The request must include valid JWT authentication credentials. The authenticated user must own the target article, which is validated by comparing the user's ID against the article's authorId field. The article must also be in an active (non-deleted) state.

The request body supports simultaneous add and remove operations, allowing users to replace attachments in a single API call. When attachments are removed, the corresponding database records and stored files are deleted.

Successful operation returns the updated list of all attachments associated with the article after applying the requested changes.

**Authentication Required**: This operation requires valid JWT authentication. Guests cannot modify article attachments.

**Ownership Validation**: Users can only modify attachments on articles they have created. Attempting to modify another user's article will result in a 403 Forbidden error.

**Related Operations**:
- `GET /articles/{articleId}` - Retrieve article details including attachment information
- `GET /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId}` - Retrieve specific attachment details
- `DELETE /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId}` - Delete individual attachment (alternative to batch remove)
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication - user must be logged in
2. Retrieve article by articleId from economic_political_board_articles table
3. Validate article exists - return 404 if not found

5. If attachmentId array provided in remove list:

operations.description:
Delete a specific file attachment from an article in the economic/political discussion board.

This operation permanently removes a single attachment file and its metadata from the system. The requester must be the owner of the parent article or have administrator privileges to delete attachments.

The deletion is immediate and irreversible. When an attachment is deleted, the file is removed from storage and the database record is marked as deleted via soft delete (deleted_at timestamp).

**Authorization Requirements**:

- Article owner: Users can only delete attachments from articles they created
- Administrator: Admins can delete attachments from any article regardless of ownership
- Guest and non-owner members: Request will be rejected with 403 Forbidden

**Deletion Behavior**:

- The attachment file is permanently removed from object storage
- Database record is soft-deleted (deleted_at timestamp set)
- Associated file metadata (filename, URL, type) is preserved in audit trail

**Related Operations**:

- `GET /articles/{articleId}` - View article details including all attachments
- `GET /articles/{articleId}/attachments` - List all attachments on an article
- `POST /articles/{articleId}/attachments` - Add new attachments to an article

1. Retrieve the article by articleId and verify attachment belongs to it
2. Check authentication and authorization:

   - If authenticated as admin → allow deletion
   - Otherwise return 403 Forbidden
3. Verify attachmentId matches the requested attachment
4. Verify attachment exists and is not already soft-deleted
5. Delete the file from object storage (physical deletion)
6. Update attachment record: set deleted_at to current timestamp
7. Update article.updated_at to reflect modification
8. Return 200 OK with deleted attachment summary data

**Database Transaction**:
- Begin transaction
- Lock article row for update (optimistic locking)
- Update attachment set deleted_at = NOW() where id = attachmentId
- Update articles set updated_at = NOW() where id = articleId
- Commit transaction

**Error Handling**:
- 404 Not Found: Article or attachment does not exist
- 403 Forbidden: User lacks ownership or admin privileges
- 409 Conflict: Attachment already deleted
- 500 Internal Server Error: File deletion from storage failed

**Security Considerations**:
- Verify user authentication token is valid
- Cross-check article author_id with authenticated user ID
- Admin role verification against economic_political_board_administrator_roles table
- Prevent path traversal or ID manipulation attacks

- Only the comment author can update their own comment

   - If not owner, return 403 Forbidden

   - Ensure comment.articleId matches the path parameter articleId
   - If mismatch, return 404 Not Found

5. Verify edit window:
   - Calculate time difference between current time and comment.createdAt
   - If exceeded time window (e.g., 60 minutes), return 409 Conflict

6. Check user ban status:
   - Verify authenticated user is not banned (isBanned = false)
   - If banned, return 403 Forbidden

7. Validate request body:
   - Ensure content field is provided and not empty
   - Validate content length against business rules (min 1, max 10000 characters)
   - Sanitize content for security (remove prohibited patterns)

8. Update comment record:
   - Set content field to new value
   - Set updatedAt to current timestamp
   - Execute database transaction

9. Return updated comment:
   - Return full IComment with updated content and timestamps
   - Include author's display name via profile join

operations.specification:
Execute soft deletion of the comment by setting deleted_at to current timestamp.

Preconditions:
1. Verify comment exists in economic_political_board_comments table
2. Verify comment belongs to the specified article (article_id matches)
3. Verify requesting user is the comment author (author_id matches authenticated user's ID)

Business Logic:
- Only the comment author can delete their own comment
- If user attempts to delete another user's comment, reject with 403 Forbidden
- If comment does not exist, reject with 404 Not Found
- If comment is already deleted, reject with 410 Gone
- If article ID does not match the comment's article, reject with 400 Bad Request

Soft Deletion Process:
- Set deleted_at to current timestamp (UTC)
- Keep comment data intact for audit trail
- Update updated_at timestamp
- Delete is permanent in terms of API visibility (not recoverable through normal operations)

Database Operation:
```sql
UPDATE economic_political_board_comments
SET deleted_at = NOW(), updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = :commentId
  AND article_id = :articleId
  AND author_id = :userId
  AND deleted_at IS NULL;
```

Error Handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: No valid authentication token
- 403 Forbidden: Comment does not belong to authenticated user
- 404 Not Found: Comment or article does not exist
- 410 Gone: Comment is already deleted

Related Operations:
- GET /articles/{articleId}/comments - List all non-deleted comments on article
- PUT /comments/{commentId} - Update own comment
- DELETE /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} - Delete comment (this operation)

Security Notes:
- Authentication required (member or admin role)
- No authorization for guests to delete comments
- Comment authorship is verified against authenticated user ID
- Cascading delete rules ensure data integrity on parent entity deletion

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of pending administrator role escalation requests for review by super administrators.

This endpoint provides comprehensive access to all administrator requests currently in 'pending' status, showing the requesting user's display name, email address, the reason provided for the administrator access request, and the submission date and time.

Super administrators can filter requests by submission date ranges, search within request reasons, and sort results by various criteria including submission date (newest first) or user information.

Each request in the list represents a member seeking promotion from regular member to administrator privileges. Upon approval, the requesting user's role will be upgraded via the economic_political_board_administrator_roles entity. Pending requests that are rejected remain in the system for audit purposes with a 'rejected' status.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering pending administrator requests

responseBody.description: Paginated list of pending administrator request summaries

operations.specification:
Query the economic_political_board_administrator_requests table with the following constraints and logic:

1. Authorization: Verify the current authenticated user has super administrator privileges. Reject with 403 Forbidden if the user is a regular administrator or member.

2. Status Filter: Automatically filter to only include requests where status = 'pending'. Do not return requests that have already been approved or rejected.

3. Join Operations: LEFT JOIN with economic_political_board_administrator_roles (user entity) to retrieve the requesting user's display_name and email fields.

4. Filtering Options:
   - Date Range Filter: Support filtering by created_at between (startDate) and created_at to (endDate)
   - Search Filter: Support text search on reason field using LIKE with wildcards for partial matching
   - Sort Options: Support sorting by created_at (DESC default for newest first), display_name (ASC/DESC), or reason (ASC/DESC)

5. Pagination: Implement cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size (default: 20, max: 100). Return total count, current page, page size, and total pages in pagination metadata.

6. Response Fields: Return only essential summary fields for list display:
   - id: UUID of the request
   - userId: UUID of the requesting user
   - displayName: User's display name
   - email: User's email address
   - reason: The submitted reason text
   - createdAt: Submission timestamp

7. Empty Results: When no pending requests match the filter criteria, return an empty data array with pagination metadata showing zero total records.

8. Error Handling:
   - Return 401 Unauthorized if user is not authenticated
   - Return 403 Forbidden if user does not have super administrator privileges
   - Return 400 Bad Request if pagination parameters are invalid (negative page, page size > 100, etc.)
   - Return 400 Bad Request if date range parameters are malformed

9. Audit: Log all access to this endpoint for security auditing, recording the requesting super administrator's ID, timestamp, and query parameters used.

10. Performance: Ensure indexes on status and created_at fields are utilized for efficient filtering. Add composite index on (status, created_at) if not already present.

operations.description:

This operation allows super administrators to grant administrator access to members who have submitted escalation requests with a valid reason. Upon approval, the system automatically promotes the user from member to regular administrator status.

The request status changes from 'pending' to 'approved', and the system records the approval timestamp (reviewed_at) and the ID of the super administrator who performed the approval (reviewed_by_admin_id) for audit trail purposes.

Only super administrators have authorization to use this endpoint. Regular administrators cannot approve or view pending administrator requests.

Check that the requesting user (user_id foreign key) is not already a banned user. If banned, reject the approval.

When a request is rejected, the requesting member remains at their current member level without gaining administrator privileges, and they are free to submit a new request if desired.

The rejection is recorded atomically with the timestamp and optional review notes documenting the super administrator's decision rationale. This audit trail helps maintain transparency and accountability in the administrator promotion process.

operations.description:
Promotes a regular administrator to super administrator status within the Economic/Political Discussion Board system.

This operation changes the grade of the specified administrator from 'regular' to 'super', granting elevated privileges including the ability to promote/demote other administrators. The promotion is recorded with the current administrator's ID as the promoter and the current timestamp.

Only super administrators can perform this operation. The system explicitly prevents self-promotion (super administrators cannot promote themselves) and rejects attempts to promote administrators who already have super grade or those without administrator status.

Successful promotion updates the administrator role record with the new grade level, records the promoting administrator's ID in the promoted_by_user_id field, and sets the promoted_at timestamp to the current time.

Related operations:
- GET /administrators - View all administrators and their current grades
- POST /administrators/{adminId}/demote - Demote super administrator to regular administrator
- PATCH /admin-requests/{requestId}/approve - Approve new administrator requests
operations.name: promote
operations.specification:
Query economic_political_board_administrator_roles to verify:
1. Current authenticated user has grade='super' (authorization check)
2. Target administrator with id=adminId exists
3. Target administrator's grade is 'regular' (not already super)
4. Target administrator ID is NOT equal to current user ID (self-promotion prevention)

Business logic:
1. Update the target administrator's grade from 'regular' to 'super'
2. Set promoted_by_user_id to the current user's ID
3. Set promoted_at to the current timestamp
4. Persist changes to the database within a transaction
5. Return the updated administrator role record

Error handling:
- Return 403 Forbidden if current user is not a super administrator
- Return 404 Not Found if administrator with adminId does not exist
- Return 400 Bad Request if target already has super grade
- Return 400 Bad Request if attempting self-promotion
- Return 400 Bad Request if target is not an administrator

responseBody.description: The updated administrator role with super grade privileges

operations.description:
Demotes a super administrator to regular administrator grade.

This operation changes an administrator's grade from 'super' to 'regular', removing their elevated privileges including the ability to promote/demote other administrators.

SECURITY REQUIREMENTS:
- Only super administrators can execute this operation
- Super administrators CANNOT demote themselves
- The target administrator must currently hold 'super' grade
- The operation records which super administrator performed the demotion

BUSINESS CONTEXT:
Administrator grade management is restricted to super administrators only. A super administrator maintains the authority to manage other super administrators' privileges, ensuring proper oversight of administrative access. When a super administrator is demoted, they retain all regular administrator capabilities including section management, content moderation, and user banning.

RELATED OPERATIONS:
- This operation requires the administrator to have 'super' grade (checked via GET /administrators/{adminId})
- Demotion action is logged for audit trail purposes
- Super administrator requests are managed via /admin/requests endpoints

VALIDATION RULES:
- Requester must have grade='super'
- Target administrator must have grade='super' before demotion
- Requester adminId cannot match target adminId
- Target must be an existing administrator
operations.name: demote
operations.specification:
1. VERIFY AUTHORIZATION: Check current authenticated user exists in economic_political_board_administrator_roles with grade='super'
2. VALIDATE TARGET: Verify administrator with {adminId} exists in economic_political_board_administrator_roles with grade='super'
3. SELF-DEMOTE CHECK: Reject if {adminId} equals current user's admin role ID
4. UPDATE GRADE: Update the record's grade field from 'super' to 'regular'
5. UPDATE AUDIT: Set promoted_by_user_id to current user's admin role ID (optional, for tracking)
6. RETURN: Return the updated economic_political_board_administrator_roles record
7. LOG: Record the demotion action in audit trail if available

ERROR HANDLING:
- 403 Forbidden: Requester is not super administrator
- 404 Not Found: Target administrator does not exist or does not have 'super' grade
- 409 Conflict: Attempting to demote self
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid adminId format

responseBody.description: Updated administrator role record with grade changed to 'regular'

Retrieve comprehensive analytics and statistical data for a specific section of the economic/political discussion board.

This endpoint provides insights into section performance and engagement metrics, including article counts, comment statistics, recent activity trends, and tag distribution patterns. The data is computed on-demand from the economic_political_board_articles and related tables.

GUESTS AND REGISTERED USERS CAN access section analytics to understand topic popularity and engagement levels. ANALYTICS DATA IS SHOWN PUBLICLY to encourage participation in popular topics.

The endpoint supports flexible filtering via request body to control which metrics are returned and the time range of analysis. This enables efficient queries for different use cases such as dashboard widgets or trend analysis.

operations.specification:
Query economic_political_board_sections by sectionId to verify section exists and is not soft-deleted.

Compute the following analytics metrics:
- Article count: Count of non-deleted articles where sectionId matches
- Comment count: Sum of commentCount from all articles in section
- Active authors: Count of distinct authorIds from articles
- Recent activity: Articles created within last 30 days
- Tag distribution: Count of articles per unique tag (top 10)
- Date range filtering: Only include articles where createdAt >= requested startDate

If startDate is not provided, default to 90 days ago.

If metricFilter is provided, only return metrics in the filter array (e.g., ['articleCount', 'commentCount', 'recentActivity']).

Return analytics data in a single JSON response with metadata about computation time.

Handle soft-deleted sections gracefully: return 404 with error if section.deleted_at is not null.

Optimize query with indexes on section.created_at and article.section_id.

operations.description:
Search and filter articles in the economic/political discussion board by title, content, tags, and/or section.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities across all articles in the system. Users can search by text keywords in article titles and content, filter by specific tags using the "tag:" prefix, filter by section, apply pagination, and sort results by creation date.

Search validation ensures query terms are between 2 and 100 characters. Results are paginated with a maximum of 50 articles per page. Default sorting is by newest first, with an option to sort by oldest first.

Tag-based searching uses the "tag:" prefix (e.g., "tag:economy") to search exclusively by tags. Partial tag name matching and autocomplete suggestions are supported through the tag search functionality.
operations.name: search
operations.specification:
Query the economic_political_board_articles table with the following logic:

1. Validate search query length (2-100 characters). Reject queries outside this range with a 400 error.

2. Parse the query string to extract:
   - Text search terms (split by spaces, apply AND/OR logic as needed)
   - Tag filters (extract tags with "tag:" prefix)
   - Section filter (if specified in query)

3. Construct a database query:
   - Perform text search on article.title and article.content fields using LIKE or full-text search
   - Apply tag filtering by joining with economic_political_board_article_tags and economic_political_board_tags
   - Apply section filtering by filtering on article.sectionId if sectionFilter is provided

4. Apply pagination:
   - Default page size: 20 articles per page
   - Maximum page size: 50 articles per page
   - Support cursor-based or offset-based pagination via page and pageSize parameters

5. Apply sorting:
   - Default: createdAt DESC (newest first)
   - Alternative: createdAt ASC (oldest first)
   - Controlled by sortOrder parameter

6. Return paginated results with:
   - Array of article summaries (basic fields: id, title, content preview, author info, tag list, section info, createdAt)
   - Pagination metadata (page, pageSize, totalItems, totalPages)

7. Error handling:
   - 400 Bad Request: Invalid search query length
   - 404 Not Found: Search returns no results (with empty array and zero pagination counts)

8. Authorization: All actors (guest, member, admin) can search articles. No authentication required.

9. Performance considerations:
   - Use database indexes on article.title, article.content, article.createdAt, article.sectionId
   - Use composite index on article_tags for tag-based filtering
   - Consider implementing full-text search indexing for large datasets

10. Edge cases:
    - Empty query (no search terms): Return all articles (paginated)
    - Tag not found: Return no results or search text terms only
    - Special characters in query: Escape properly, perform exact or fuzzy matching
    - Very long tag names: Handle gracefully with truncation or rejection

operations.description:
Lift an active user ban by updating the associated user's ban status.

This operation allows administrators to remove a user's ban restriction, restoring their platform access and login capabilities. The ban record itself remains in the database for audit purposes as a permanent historical record, but the associated user account is updated to reflect active status.

Only users with administrative privileges can execute this operation. Regular members and guests cannot access this endpoint. The system validates that the ban record exists and belongs to a valid user before processing the unban request.

The ban record maintains all original information including the reason for the initial ban, the administrator who issued the ban, and the original ban timestamp. These records are never deleted to ensure accountability and maintain a complete audit history of all ban actions taken on the platform.

   - Record unban timestamp (createdAtAdminId already contains banning admin)

6. Log unban action for audit trail
7. Return updated ban record with lifted status

IEconomicPoliticalBoardSection.description:
Complete section entity representing a topic categorization area in the economic/political discussion board. Sections organize articles into topic areas and can only be created and managed by administrators. Each section has a unique name that serves as its identifier and an optional description explaining its purpose.

This response type includes all section metadata including system-managed fields (timestamps, deletion status, creator reference) and the articles contained within the section. Banned sections are soft-deleted (deleted_at is set) and hidden from new article creation but remain accessible for historical reference.

Related operations:
- GET /sections: List all active sections
- GET /sections/{id}: Get single section details (this type)
- POST /sections: Create new section (admin only)
- PUT /sections/{id}: Update section (admin only)
- DELETE /sections/{id}: Soft delete section (admin only)

Join articles table filtered by sectionId and return as ISummary[] array, sorted by created_at DESC. Fields: id (UUID), name (unique string), description (nullable string), created_at (timestamptz), updated_at (timestamptz), deleted_at (nullable timestamptz for soft delete), createdByAdminId (UUID, admin reference). Include articles array with article summaries.

Filtering logic:
- startDate: ISO date-time string. If not provided, default to 90 days ago from current time. Filter articles where createdAt >= startDate.
- metricFilter: Array of strings like ['articleCount', 'commentCount', 'recentActivity', 'tagDistribution', 'activeAuthors']. If provided, only return metrics in this list. If not provided, return all metrics.
- page: Page number for pagination (default: 1). Only used if result set is large.
- limit: Items per page (default: 10, max: 100).

Computation:
1. Query economic_political_board_sections by sectionId (from path parameter)

4. If metricFilter is provided, only include metrics in the filter list

Returns top 10 most used tags in this section with article counts.

IEconomicPoliticalBoardSectionAnalytic.description:
Analytics data for a discussion section containing computed metrics and engagement statistics.

This schema represents aggregated insights about a section's activity, including article and comment counts, author participation metrics, recent engagement trends, and popular topic tags. The data is computed on-demand from multiple related tables to provide a comprehensive view of section performance.

The analytics help users understand section popularity and engagement levels, encouraging participation in active discussion topics. This endpoint is accessible to all users (guests and registered) to view publicly.
IEconomicPoliticalBoardSectionAnalytic.x-autobe-specification:
Computed analytics aggregation from multiple database tables: economic_political_board_sections, economic_political_board_articles, economic_political_board_article_tags, economic_political_board_tags, economic_political_board_comments.

Computation logic:
1. Query section by sectionId, verify exists and deleted_at IS NULL
2. section: JOIN from IEconomicPoliticalBoardSection.ISummary using sectionId
3. articleCount: COUNT(*) WHERE section_id=sectionId AND deleted_at IS NULL
4. commentCount: SUM(articles.commentCount) WHERE section_id=sectionId
5. activeAuthorCount: COUNT(DISTINCT author_id) WHERE section_id=sectionId
6. recentArticleCount: COUNT(*) WHERE section_id=sectionId AND created_at >= (NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days')
7. tagDistribution: JOIN articles->article_tags->tags, GROUP BY tag, ORDER BY count DESC, LIMIT 10

Request body filters: startDate (defaults to 90 days ago), metricFilter (selective metrics), pagination params (page, limit)

# 🧪 Generating E2E Test Suites

I'm executing the **test()** agent to generate comprehensive end-to-end test suites for all API interfaces.

instruction:
Generate E2E test suites for Economic/Political Discussion Board:

**Authentication Tests:**
- Test user registration with valid email/password
- Test user registration with duplicate email (should fail)
- Test user registration with invalid email format (should fail)
- Test user login with valid credentials
- Test user login with invalid credentials (should fail)
- Test user logout
- Test password change with valid current password
- Test password change with invalid current password (should fail)
- Test account deletion and cascade deletion of articles/comments
- Test that banned users cannot log in
- Test that current user can retrieve own profile

**Profile Tests:**
- Test getting current user's profile
- Test updating current user's profile (display name, bio)
- Test viewing another user's profile
- Test that deleted users' profiles return 404

**Section Tests:**
- Test getting list of all sections
- Test getting single section details
- Test creating section (regular user should fail with 403)
- Test creating section (admin should succeed)
- Test updating section (regular user should fail with 403)
- Test updating section (admin should succeed)
- Test deleting section (regular user should fail with 403)
- Test deleting section (admin should succeed)
- Test that deleting section cascades to related articles

**Article Tests:**
- Test creating article with valid title, content, section, and tags
- Test creating article with missing required fields (should fail)
- Test creating article with file attachment
- Test creating article with image attachment
- Test getting list of articles in a section (paginated)
- Test sorting articles by newest first
- Test sorting articles by oldest first
- Test getting single article details
- Test editing own article
- Test editing another user's article (should fail with 403)
- Test deleting own article
- Test deleting another user's article (should fail with 403)
- Test admin deleting any article
- Test searching articles by title
- Test searching articles by content
- Test filtering search results by tags
- Test that deleted articles are not returned in searches

**Comment Tests:**
- Test creating comment on article
- Test creating comment with empty content (should fail)
- Test getting all comments on an article (sorted oldest first)
- Test editing own comment
- Test editing another user's comment (should fail with 403)
- Test deleting own comment
- Test deleting another user's comment (should fail with 403)
- Test admin deleting any comment
- Test that nested comments are not allowed (single-level only)

**Administrator Tests:**
- Test user submitting admin request
- Test super admin viewing pending admin requests
- Test super admin approving admin request
- Test super admin rejecting admin request
- Test regular admin trying to approve request (should fail with 403)
- Test promoting regular admin to super admin
- Test demoting super admin to regular admin
- Test super admin attempting to demote themselves (should fail with 403)

**Ban Management Tests:**
- Test admin banning a user with reason
- Test banned user attempting to log in (should fail with 403)
- Test admin unbanning a user
- Test banning user who is already banned (should fail with 403)
- Test unblocking user who is not banned (should fail with 403)
- Test getting list of all banned users with ban reasons
- Test that banned user's articles and comments remain visible
- Test that regular users cannot ban/unban other users (should fail with 403)

**Pagination & Sorting Tests:**
- Test pagination limits and offsets for article list
- Test pagination limits and offsets for comment list
- Test pagination limits and offsets for section list
- Test pagination limits and offsets for banned users list
- Test invalid pagination parameters (negative numbers, zero, etc.)

**Error Handling Tests:**
- Test 401 Unauthorized for unauthenticated requests
- Test 403 Forbidden for unauthorized actions
- Test 404 Not Found for non-existent resources
- Test 400 Bad Request for validation errors
- Test 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures
- Test all validation error messages are clear and helpful

**Edge Case Tests:**
- Test empty database state
- Test user with no articles or comments
- Test section with no articles
- Test article with no comments
- Test article with many attachments (multiple files and images)
- Test article with many tags
- Test comment with very long content
- Test article title/content with special characters
- Test simultaneous article creation (race conditions)
- Test admin role changes and verify permissions update immediately

scenario.draft: Test successful guest user registration with valid email and password. The test should send a POST request to /economicPoliticalBoard/auth/guest/join with a valid unique email address, a password meeting minimum requirements (at least 8 characters), and required session context (href, referrer, ip). The system should validate the email format, check that the email is not already registered, hash the password using bcrypt, create a User record in the database with isBanned set to false, automatically create a corresponding Profile record with the display name defaulted from the email prefix and an empty bio, and return JWT access and refresh tokens. The response should include the user ID, authentication token object with access and refresh tokens, and expiration timestamps. Validate that both User and Profile records were created successfully in the database with correct values.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /economicPoliticalBoard/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

scenario.draft: Test user registration with a custom display name provided during the registration request. The test should send a POST request to /economicPoliticalBoard/auth/guest/join with valid email, valid password, and an optional displayName parameter containing a custom display name (up to 50 characters). The system should validate the displayName length, create the User record, and create a Profile record with the provided display name instead of generating a default from the email prefix. The test should verify that the Profile record was created with the exact custom display name provided, and that the display name appears correctly when retrieving the user's profile. This validates that optional profile fields are handled correctly during the registration flow.

scenario.draft:
Test that profile is automatically created during registration with correct data linkage:

1. Send registration request:
   - POST /economicPoliticalBoard/auth/member/join with:
     - email: 'profiletest@example.com'
     - valid password
     - displayName: 'Test User Display Name'
     - bio: 'This is a test bio description'
     - href: 'https://example.com/register'
     - referrer: 'https://example.com/home'
     - ip: '127.0.0.1'

2. Verify registration success (HTTP 200) with JWT tokens

3. Retrieve the newly created user's profile:
   - Query economic_political_board_profiles table by userId
   - Verify the userId matches the user ID from registration response
   - Verify all profile fields are correctly stored:
     - displayName: 'Test User Display Name'
     - bio: 'This is a test bio description'
   - Verify no other profile records exist for this user

4. Test with minimal profile data (empty bio):
   - Register second user with displayName but empty bio
   - Verify profile is created with empty bio field
   - Verify database accepts null or empty string for bio

5. Test with no bio field provided:
   - Register third user with displayName only (omit bio from request)
   - Verify profile is created with default empty bio
   - Verify system handles missing optional bio gracefully

6. Verify profile-viewing behavior:
   - Use access token to call profile retrieval endpoint
   - Verify returned profile matches what was created
   - Verify other users can view this profile (public visibility)

7. Verify profile is linked correctly:
   - economic_political_board_profiles.userId foreign key points to economic_political_board_users.id
   - Cascade delete: if user is deleted, profile is also deleted (verify referential integrity)

scenario.draft:
This test scenario validates the primary success path for retrieving a paginated list of all available tags in the economic/political discussion board system.

**Test Steps**:
1. Call the `/economicPoliticalBoard/tags` endpoint with default pagination parameters (page=1, limit=50, no search term)
2. Verify the response returns a valid paginated structure with `pagination` and `data` fields
3. Verify pagination metadata is correct: `current` page equals 1, `limit` equals 50, `records` equals total tag count, `pages` equals calculated total pages
4. Verify all returned tags contain required fields: `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
5. Verify tag names are lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens only
6. Verify tags are sorted alphabetically by name in ascending order by default
7. Verify no soft-deleted tags are included (all tags have valid entries)
8. Call the endpoint again with `limit=200` (maximum allowed) and verify it returns more tags or the same all tags
9. Call with `page=2` and verify it returns the next page of tags without overlapping with page 1

**Validation Points**:
- Response status code is 200 OK
- Pagination metadata accurately reflects the total records and current page position
- Each tag in the `data` array has valid UUID for id, lowercase name pattern, and ISO datetime for created_at and updated_at
- Tags are returned in alphabetical order by name
- The `data` array is non-empty when tags exist in the system
- Pagination correctly handles edge cases (single page, exact page boundaries)

- Both ascending and descending order options work correctly
- Pagination accurately tracks current page, total records, and total pages

Test that an administrator cannot ban a user who is already banned - duplicate ban attempts should be rejected.

scenario.draft:
This test validates the primary success path for the unban user operation.

**Test Flow:**
1. Regular administrator joins via /auth/admin/join to obtain admin credentials
2. Member joins via /auth/member/join to create the user who will be banned
3. Admin bans the member via POST /economicPoliticalBoard/admin/ban-records with reason to create a ban record
4. Admin calls PATCH /economicPoliticalBoard/admin/ban-records/{banRecordId}/unban with the ban record ID
5. Verify the ban record status changes from 'active' to 'lifted' in the response
6. Verify the associated user's isBanned flag is set to false
7. Verify the user can immediately log in with their credentials (restored access)
8. Verify the ban record still contains original ban reason and banning admin information for audit trail

**Validation Points:**
- Ban record status transitions from active to lifted
- User's isBanned field changes to false
- User can successfully authenticate immediately after unban
- Ban record maintains all historical data (reason, original timestamp, banning admin ID)
- Response returns IEconomicPoliticalBoardBanRecord.ISummary with updated status

scenario.draft:
This test validates that users maintain their session when unbanned while logged in, as specified in the User Unban Process business rules.

**Test Flow:**
1. Administrator joins via /auth/admin/join (creates admin account with session)
2. Member user joins via /auth/member/join (creates member account)
3. Member user logs in via /auth/member/login (establishes active session with valid access token)
4. Admin bans the member user via POST /economicPoliticalBoard/admin/ban-records with a reason
5. Admin unbans the member user via PATCH /economicPoliticalBoard/admin/ban-records/{banRecordId}/unban while the member still has active session
6. Verify the ban record status changes to 'lifted'
7. Verify the member can continue using their existing access token without re-authentication (session maintained)
8. Verify the member can access protected resources with the same session token

**Validation Points:**
- Ban record status transitions to lifted
- User's isBanned field is set to false
- User's existing access token remains valid after unban
- User does not need to re-authenticate to continue their session
- User can access articles, comments, and profile with original token

**Business Rule Validation:**
- IF the user is currently logged in when unbanned, THE system SHALL maintain their current session
- Immediate restoration of login capability while preserving active sessions

scenario.draft:
This test validates business rule error handling when attempting to unban users who are not currently banned.

**Test Flow**:
1. Admin joins via /auth/admin/join
2. Member user joins via /auth/member/join (not banned, no ban record exists)
3. Admin attempts to call PATCH /economicPoliticalBoard/admin/ban-records/{banRecordId}/unban with an invalid/non-existent ban record ID
4. Verify the system rejects the request with 404 Not Found
5. Verify the error indicates the ban record does not exist
6. Verify no state changes occur (member's isBanned flag remains false)

**Validation Points**:
- System rejects unban attempt on non-existent ban record (404 Not Found)
- Appropriate error response with clear message
- User's isBanned flag remains unchanged

**Business Rule Validation**:
- IF no ban record exists for the user, THE system SHALL return 404 Not Found
- Ban records are immutable except for status updates on unban
- All ban records must remain in system for audit purposes even after unbanning

# 💻 Implementing Business Logic

I'm executing the **realize()** agent to implement the actual business logic for all API endpoints. This agent will create fully functional service provider code with validation, security checks, and business rules.

instruction:
Implement business logic for Economic/Political Discussion Board:

**Authentication Services:**
- Register users with email validation and password hashing
- Login with email/password verification and JWT token generation
- Implement token refresh mechanism
- Change password with current password verification
- Delete account with cascade delete of user's articles and comments
- Banned user login rejection with 403 Forbidden error
- Retrieve current user info with authorization middleware

**Profile Services:**
- Get current user profile
- Update user's display name and bio
- Validate displayName (1-50 characters, no special characters)
- Validate bio (0-500 characters)
- Get another user's profile by user ID
- Handle 404 for non-existent users

**Section Services:**
- List all sections (paginated, default 20 per page)
- Get single section details
- Create section (admin only) with name and description
- Update section (admin only) with validation
- Delete section (admin only) with cascade to related articles
- Validate section name uniqueness
- Handle 403 for non-admin users

**Article Services:**
- List articles in a section (paginated, sortable by newest/oldest)
- Get single article details with author info
- Create article with validation (title required, content required, section required)
- Handle file attachments (files and images separately)
- Handle tag creation and linking (many-to-many with Tag entity)
- Update own article (validation only for own articles)
- Delete own article (validation only for own articles)
- Admin can delete any article
- Search articles by title or content (full-text search)
- Filter search results by tags
- Return article count with comment count
- Handle 403 for unauthorized article modifications
- Handle 404 for non-existent articles

**Comment Services:**
- List all comments on an article (sorted oldest first, paginated)
- Create comment on article (content required, article must exist)
- Update own comment only
- Delete own comment only
- Admin can delete any comment
- Single-level comments only (no nested replies)
- Validate comment content length (1-1000 characters)
- Handle 403 for unauthorized comment modifications
- Handle 404 for non-existent comments/articles

**Administrator Services:**
- List pending admin requests (super admin only)
- Approve admin request (promote user to regular admin) (super admin only)
- Reject admin request (delete request record) (super admin only)
- Promote regular admin to super admin (super admin only)
- Demote super admin to regular admin (super admin cannot demote themselves)
- Verify admin role and grade before actions
- Handle 403 for unauthorized admin operations

**Ban Management Services:**
- Ban user with reason (admin only)
- Unban user (admin only)
- Check if user is already banned (prevent duplicate bans)
- Check if user is not banned (prevent unbanning non-banned users)
- List all banned users with ban reasons and ban dates (admin only)
- Verify ban status on login
- Verify ban status prevents API access
- Banned users' articles and comments remain visible to all users

**Attachment Services:**
- Upload file attachments (multiple files per article)
- Upload image attachments (multiple images per article)
- Store file URLs in database
- Generate download URLs for attachments
- Handle file type validation (images: jpg, jpeg, png, gif; files: any)
- Handle 404 for non-existent attachments

**Search Services:**
- Full-text search across article title and content
- Paginated search results (default 20 per page)
- Filter search results by tags (multiple tags allowed)
- Return article snippets matching search query
- Return hit count and pagination info

**Error Handling:**
- 400 Bad Request for validation errors
- 401 Unauthorized for missing/invalid tokens
- 403 Forbidden for unauthorized actions (banned, non-admin, not owner)
- 404 Not Found for non-existent resources
- 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures
- Consistent error response format with message, code, and timestamp

**Security:**
- Password hashing with bcrypt
- JWT token validation and refresh
- CORS configuration
- Rate limiting for authentication endpoints
- Input validation for all endpoints
- SQL injection prevention through Prisma ORM
- XSS prevention for content fields

**Validation:**
- Email format validation
- Password strength validation (minimum 8 characters)
- Display name validation (1-50 characters, alphanumeric)
- Content length validation
- Required field validation
- Unique constraint validation
- Foreign key constraint validation
- Cascading delete validation

**Business Rules:**
- Users can only edit/delete their own content (except admins)
- Super admins have full control over all admins
- Admin requests require super admin approval
- Banned users cannot create new content
- Deleted users' profiles return 404
- Cascade delete all user data on account deletion
- Admin grades are immutable once set (except by super admin)
- Demotion requires valid target user and grade

import { TypedBody, TypedParam, TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

import { IEconomicPoliticalBoardArticle } from "../../../../api/structures/IEconomicPoliticalBoardArticle";
import { IPageIEconomicPoliticalBoardArticle } from "../../../../api/structures/IPageIEconomicPoliticalBoardArticle";
import { GuestAuth } from "../../../../decorators/GuestAuth";
import { GuestPayload } from "../../../../decorators/payload/GuestPayload";
import { getEconomicPoliticalBoardGuestArticlesArticleId } from "../../../../providers/getEconomicPoliticalBoardGuestArticlesArticleId";
import { patchEconomicPoliticalBoardGuestArticles } from "../../../../providers/patchEconomicPoliticalBoardGuestArticles";
import { patchEconomicPoliticalBoardGuestArticlesSearch } from "../../../../providers/patchEconomicPoliticalBoardGuestArticlesSearch";

@Controller("/economicPoliticalBoard/guest/articles")
export class EconomicpoliticalboardGuestArticlesController {
  /**
   * Retrieve a single article's full content and metadata by its unique identifier.
   *
   * This operation returns complete article details including the title, body content, author information (administrator grade and promotion details from the administrator roles table), section assignment (name and description), associated file attachments with download URLs, and tags for content categorization. The response provides all information needed for article display in the user interface.
   *
   * Articles are stored with soft deletion support via the deleted_at field. This operation only returns articles that have not been soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). If the specified article ID does not exist, has been soft-deleted, or belongs to a deleted section, the operation returns a 404 Not Found error.
   *
   * Authorization levels:
   * - Guests: Can view public articles (all articles are publicly readable)
   * - Members: Can view all articles including their own
   * - Administrators: Can view all articles with additional management capabilities
   *
   * Related operations:
   * - GET /sections/:id - Retrieve the section this article belongs to for navigation context
   * - GET /articles/:id/comments - Retrieve all comments on this article for discussion viewing
   * - PUT /articles/:id - Update this article (author only)
   * - DELETE /articles/:id - Remove this article (author only)
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param articleId Unique identifier of the article to retrieve
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor guest
   * @x-autobe-specification Query economic_political_board_articles table for single article by UUID.
   *
   * Implementation steps:
   * 1. Validate articleId parameter is valid UUID format
   * 2. Query economic_political_board_articles WHERE id = :articleId AND deleted_at IS NULL
   * 3. If no record found, return 404 Not Found
   * 4. Load related data:
   *    - Join with economic_political_board_administrator_roles to get author display name
   *    - Join with economic_political_board_sections to get section name and description
   *    - Query economic_political_board_attachments WHERE article_id = :articleId AND deleted_at IS NULL
   *    - Query economic_political_board_article_tags WHERE article_id = :articleId
   *    - For each tag, join with economic_political_board_tags to get tag name
   * 5. Assemble response with article data, author info, section info, attachments array, and tags array
   * 6. Return 200 OK with full article object
   *
   * Error handling:
   * - 404: Article not found or soft-deleted
   * - 400: Invalid UUID format in articleId parameter
   *
   * Transaction: Single query with eager loading of related data. No writes involved.
   *
   * Security: No special authorization checks needed as articles are publicly readable. Authorization middleware handles access level validation for any future protected features.
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Get(":articleId")
  public async at(
    @GuestAuth()
    guest: GuestPayload,
    @TypedParam("articleId")
    articleId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
  ): Promise<IEconomicPoliticalBoardArticle> {
    try {
      return await getEconomicPoliticalBoardGuestArticlesArticleId({
        guest,
        articleId,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of articles from the economic/political discussion board.
   *
   * This operation returns summarized article information with support for advanced search and filtering capabilities. Articles that are soft-deleted (deleted_at is set) are excluded from results by default. Results can be filtered by section, searched by text, sorted by various criteria, and paginated for efficient data retrieval.
   *
   * The operation supports filtering by section ID to retrieve articles within a specific topic area. Full-text search on article title and content uses PostgreSQL's GIN indexes for efficient text matching. Tag filtering allows retrieving articles associated with specific tags through the article-tag junction table.
   *
   * Results are sorted by creation date (newest first) by default, but alternative sorting criteria are supported including title, author, and update date. Pagination uses cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Search criteria and pagination parameters for article list retrieval.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor guest
   * @x-autobe-specification Query economic_political_board_articles table with the following logic:
   *
   * 1. **Soft Delete Filtering**: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL to exclude soft-deleted articles
   *
   * 2. **Section Filtering**: If section_id is provided in request body, add WHERE section_id = :section_id to filter articles within a specific topic category
   *
   * 3. **Tag Filtering**: If tag_id is provided, join with economic_political_board_article_tags and filter WHERE tag_id = :tag_id to find articles associated with a specific tag
   *
   * 4. **Full-Text Search**: If search text is provided, use PostgreSQL tsquery/tsvector or ILIKE pattern matching on title and content columns. Utilize the existing GIN indexes on title(ops: gin_trgm_ops) and content(ops: gin_trgm_ops) for efficient text search
   *
   * 5. **Sorting**: Apply ORDER BY clause based on sort field:
   *    - created_at DESC (default): Sort by creation date, newest first
   *    - updated_at DESC: Sort by last update date, most recently updated first
   *    - title ASC/DESC: Sort alphabetically by title
   *    - author_id ASC/DESC: Sort by author ID
   *
   * 6. **Pagination**: Implement cursor-based or offset-based pagination:
   *    - Use page and pageSize parameters
   *    - Apply LIMIT :pageSize OFFSET :offset
   *    - Return total count for pagination metadata
   *
   * 7. **Result Projection**: Select only necessary fields for summary view:
   *    - id, title, author_id, section_id, created_at, updated_at
   *    - Exclude content field to reduce response size (use individual article endpoint for full content)
   *
   * 8. **Authorization**: Public read access - no authentication required. All articles are visible to guests and members.
   *
   * 9. **Error Handling**: Return 400 if pagination parameters are invalid (page < 1, pageSize outside bounds). Return 404 if section_id or tag_id references non-existent entities (when provided).
   *
   * **Performance Considerations**:
   * - Leverage indexes on section_id, created_at, title, and content
   * - For tag filtering, use EXISTS subquery or JOIN with economic_political_board_article_tags
   * - Avoid N+1 queries by pre-loading section and author information if included in summary
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async index(
    @GuestAuth()
    guest: GuestPayload,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IEconomicPoliticalBoardArticle.IRequest,
  ): Promise<IPageIEconomicPoliticalBoardArticle.ISummary> {
    try {
      return await patchEconomicPoliticalBoardGuestArticles({
        guest,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Search and filter articles in the economic/political discussion board by title, content, tags, and/or section.
   *
   * This operation provides advanced search capabilities across all articles in the system. Users can search by text keywords in article titles and content, filter by specific tags using the "tag:" prefix, filter by section, apply pagination, and sort results by creation date.
   *
   * Search validation ensures query terms are between 2 and 100 characters. Results are paginated with a maximum of 50 articles per page. Default sorting is by newest first, with an option to sort by oldest first.
   *
   * Tag-based searching uses the "tag:" prefix (e.g., "tag:economy") to search exclusively by tags. Partial tag name matching and autocomplete suggestions are supported through the tag search functionality.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Search criteria and pagination parameters
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor guest
   * @x-autobe-specification Query the economic_political_board_articles table with the following logic:
   *
   * 1. Validate search query length (2-100 characters). Reject queries outside this range with a 400 error.
   *
   * 2. Parse the query string to extract:
   *    - Text search terms (split by spaces, apply AND/OR logic as needed)
   *    - Tag filters (extract tags with "tag:" prefix)
   *    - Section filter (if specified in query)
   *
   * 3. Construct a database query:
   *    - Perform text search on article.title and article.content fields using LIKE or full-text search
   *    - Apply tag filtering by joining with economic_political_board_article_tags and economic_political_board_tags
   *    - Apply section filtering by filtering on article.sectionId if sectionFilter is provided
   *
   * 4. Apply pagination:
   *    - Default page size: 20 articles per page
   *    - Maximum page size: 50 articles per page
   *    - Support cursor-based or offset-based pagination via page and pageSize parameters
   *
   * 5. Apply sorting:
   *    - Default: createdAt DESC (newest first)
   *    - Alternative: createdAt ASC (oldest first)
   *    - Controlled by sortOrder parameter
   *
   * 6. Return paginated results with:
   *    - Array of article summaries (basic fields: id, title, content preview, author info, tag list, section info, createdAt)
   *    - Pagination metadata (page, pageSize, totalItems, totalPages)
   *
   * 7. Error handling:
   *    - 400 Bad Request: Invalid search query length
   *    - 404 Not Found: Search returns no results (with empty array and zero pagination counts)
   *
   * 8. Authorization: All actors (guest, member, admin) can search articles. No authentication required.
   *
   * 9. Performance considerations:
   *    - Use database indexes on article.title, article.content, article.createdAt, article.sectionId
   *    - Use composite index on article_tags for tag-based filtering
   *    - Consider implementing full-text search indexing for large datasets
   *
   * 10. Edge cases:
   *     - Empty query (no search terms): Return all articles (paginated)
   *     - Tag not found: Return no results or search text terms only
   *     - Special characters in query: Escape properly, perform exact or fuzzy matching
